I've been working this land for forty years. I know this soil, I know the weather, I know what my neighbors do, and I know what has fed my family and paid my bills. My son works in the city now so it's mostly just me managing the farm. I have to be practical about labor.

**My thinking:**

The wheat-maize rotation on the flat fields is the backbone — I put about 8 mu into that. I've been planting Jimai-series wheat here for years, it does well in our soil. For maize I'll use Xianyu 335 hybrid seed, nearly everyone around here uses it, yields are reliable. I plant maize right after wheat harvest without plowing — the machine plants straight into the stubble, saves me time and the ground doesn't need it anyway.

The other 4.4 mu I keep in cotton. Cotton is more work — spraying, pruning, picking — but it brings in cash that wheat and maize don't always match. I use Bt hybrid cotton now, less spraying for bollworm than the old varieties, though I still spray for aphids and spider mites several times.

I water from the well. Wheat needs water at sowing, jointing, and heading — three times usually, sometimes a fourth if spring is dry. Maize I water at planting and again if August gets hot. Cotton needs more careful irrigation, especially around flowering and boll setting.

I don't use soil tests. I apply compound fertilizer as base and urea as topdressing, roughly what I've always done. More is safer in my mind.
